diagnose:orders.business: orders: Kestrel Hollow Outfitters (fictional online outdoor gear store), kestrel_hollow_orders_2026.xlsx, build a1. The grill asked 7 questions plus the build question (goal, Southwest/Southeast alias, sale_def, Order ID duplicates, channel fees, leave_out, row grain). The owner agent answered with letters only (state.json: every text field empty). The brain holds 6 owner notes, 5 counted facts, 3 insights, 2 playbook guesses and 2 open items. None of the five brief rules that decide the eval answers (percent-then-dollars discounts, # migration copies, CS reships, which statuses count, gift cards) got into the brain as a usable rule. Only gift cards and cancelled made it in, as loose words not tied to any data values. I replayed the tool on a scratch copy (Analysis plus interview.candidates with the recorded answers). After round 2 the candidate pool was empty, so the interview stopped at 7 of HARD_CAP 10 questions and wrote no open items. Detectors, not budget, were the limit. Every wrong figure the judges quoted can be reproduced exactly: Feb 23,099.64 = copies kept + CS kept + Exchanged dropped + every discount read as dollars. Feb 24,702.64 = copies kept + CS kept + dollars. Feb 22,519.64 = CS kept + dollars. Discounts 9,404.38 / 9,159.38 / 8,954.13 / 8,907.93 = the dollars reading with the same variants. The correct answers reproduce with all rules applied (Feb 22,243.65, discounts 8,483.24, Talus 45L top for Apr to Jun).

facts.fact: F1 Discount unit changes on 2026-03-02: before, it is a whole-number percent of qty x unit price. From Mar 2 on, it is dollars off the line. Blank or 0 means none.
facts.question: None. The only touch was R1 Q3 (sale_def) option 'Discounts and comps', which asks whether sales leave discounts out, not what the number means.
facts.data_signal: Before 2026-03-02, every nonzero Discount (362 lines, all KH- IDs) is one of exactly {10, 15, 20, 25}, 100% integers. From 2026-03-02 on, the 358 nonzero lines take 89 distinct values and only 28% are integers (5.4, 3.4, 9.6, 18.9, 14.1 ...). Read as dollars, 8 pre-switch lines get a discount bigger than qty x price, which is impossible (e.g. KH-20529 Fuel Canister 1 x 7.99 with Discount 25; KH-20456 Enamel Mug 1 x 18 with Discount 20). The switch date lines up exactly with two other changes. (1) The Order ID family: KH- ends 2026-03-01, # starts. (2) A blank-vs-0 convention: KH- rows use 0 on 1,450 lines and are never blank, # rows are blank on 2,150 lines and never 0. 7 of the 8 answers' February figures reproduce only with every discount read as dollars.
facts.root_cause: No detector. analyze._sign_flips only tests whether a metric's sign flips at a date. Nothing tests a change in value support, integer share or scale, or compares a discount to the row's line amount. The playbook fixes Discount's unit (sales_transactions.json roles.discount unit=currency). So brain._column_statement shows it in dollars and publishes a sum ('from $0 to $114, summing to $10.6k') that mixes two units. No playbook or finding question asks what a discount number means.
facts.code_refs: sheetbrain/analyze.py Analysis._sign_flips (381-420); sheetbrain/findings.py finding_questions signflip branch (270-291), the only date-boundary question type; playbooks/sales_transactions.json roles.discount {unit: currency}; sheetbrain/brain.py _column_statement (829-858, money formatting from role unit); sheetbrain/profile.py Col.integers (whole-column flag only)
facts.general_fix: Generalize _sign_flips into a regime-change detector for every numeric metric with a date column. Scan split dates and compare before vs after on: distinct-value count, integer share, whether values come from a small fixed set, and the ratio to any same-row amount (qty x price). Rank splits higher when they coincide with another boundary the tool found (ID-prefix change, label vocabulary change, blank-vs-0 change). Add a unit sanity check for any column a role calls money: a small integer set that sometimes exceeds the row's line amount means suspect percent. Ask one finding question with the counted evidence ('Before Mar 2, 2026 Discount is always 10, 15, 20 or 25; after, it takes 89 values like 5.40 and 18.90. What changed?') with options 'Percent before, dollars after' / 'Same unit throughout' / 'Something else (type it)'. Until the unit is confirmed, show it as unconfirmed and publish no sum.

facts.fact: F2 Migration copies: at go-live the new platform imported the Feb 27 to Mar 1 orders again. The # orders dated before Mar 2 are copies: drop them and keep the KH- originals.
facts.question: None about this. R1 Q4 ('1,111 Order ID values appear more than once (2,721 rows). Is that the same one twice?') asked about ordinary multi-line orders. The owner answered 'Different, keep both', which is right for that question. The brain then stored it as 'Rows that repeat a Order ID: different, keep both', which reads as 'no duplicates to remove'.
facts.data_signal: Order ID has two shape families. KH- has 1,796 lines, dated 2025-11-01 to 2026-03-01, with real times of day. # has 2,524 lines, dated 2026-02-27 to 2026-06-30, all at midnight. They overlap only on Feb 27, 28 and Mar 1, and lines per day double on exactly those days (14+14, 18+18, 23+23 vs about 15 on nearby days). All 28 # orders dated before Mar 2 have the same (date, SKU, qty) line set as one KH- order (e.g. #10001 = KH-21488, #10002 = KH-21489). 55 of 55 lines match on date, SKU, qty and unit price (54 also on region). Keeping them adds 2,234.95 to February.
facts.root_cause: recipes.duplicates counts repeats of one ID column. It ignores that profile.composite_key had already found Order ID + SKU unique, so it flagged ordinary multi-line orders, and findings.finding_questions framed that as 'the same one twice?'. No detector looks for the same row content under different IDs, or for two ID families overlapping in time. analyze._exclusive_prefixes builds ID-prefix families but only checks whether one dimension value owns a prefix.
facts.code_refs: sheetbrain/recipes.py duplicates (269-282); sheetbrain/findings.py duplicates branch (125-138); sheetbrain/profile.py composite_key (288-315, result unused by the duplicates finding); sheetbrain/analyze.py _exclusive_prefixes (422-471)
facts.general_fix: (1) Skip the single-column duplicates finding when a composite key containing that ID is unique, and ask about row grain instead. Word any resulting note narrowly ('Order ID repeats because each row is one line of an order'). (2) Add a content-duplicate detector: hash each row on every non-identifier column (text trimmed and case-folded, dates to the day, numbers to the cent, blank = 0), then group collisions whose IDs differ. Report the count, the ID families involved and the date window. (3) Add an ID-family timeline: split ID values by shape or prefix, compute each family's date range, and flag overlaps. Ask: '55 lines dated Feb 27 to Mar 1, 2026 appear twice, once with KH- numbers and once with # numbers (same items, quantities, prices). Which copy counts?' with options keep KH- / keep # / both are real.

facts.fact: Structure: two exports are stacked. The new export's header row repeats mid-sheet, and labels are spelled differently across the two (Online Store vs Web Store, Popup vs Pop-Up, Complete vs Fulfilled, Cancelled vs Canceled). This matters because status and channel rules must cover both spellings.
facts.question: None. The only alias question was R1 Q2 'Are "Southwest" and "Southeast" in Customer Region the same thing?', a false positive.
facts.data_signal: Excel row 1801 is a second header row: ('Order #','Created At','SKU','Item Name','Quantity','Price','Discount','Sales Channel','Order Status','Ship Region'). It puts text in the date, Qty and Unit Price columns. The vocabularies split exactly at that row. Channel: 'Online Store' (1,111) and 'Popup' (83) appear only above it; 'Web Store' (1,386, 17 with a trailing space) and 'Pop-Up' (344) only below. Status: 'Complete' (1,523) only above; 'Fulfilled', 'Shipped', 'Backordered' mostly below; 'Cancelled' 84 above vs 'Canceled' 82 below. Region: 'N/A' only above, blank only below. The tool's own alias_pairs found Pop-Up/Popup (427 rows) and Cancelled/Canceled (166) but asked only Southwest/Southeast (913 rows).
facts.root_cause: tables._build_table appends every non-empty, non-total row under the first header. It never checks for a repeated or alternate header row, so the second export merged into one table and its header became a data row: 'Sales Channel', 'Order Status' and 'Ship Region' show up as values in the brain's column nodes, and 'Order Status' is one of the '9 values' in the Status insight. interview._alias_questions slices alias_pairs(...)[:1] before skipping answered ids. Once Southwest/Southeast was answered, no other pair could ever surface. alias_pairs ranks by row volume and uses only string similarity, so renamed labels (Online Store/Web Store, Complete/Fulfilled) are invisible.
facts.code_refs: sheetbrain/tables.py _build_table (245-256); sheetbrain/interview.py alias_pairs (370-395), _alias_questions (398-419, [:1] at 400 before the answered check at 402)
facts.general_fix: In table finding, treat any in-body row with header score >= 0.5 whose typed columns (date, number) hold text as a segment boundary. Keep both header sets, profile each segment, and write a counted structure fact ('rows 5-1800 and 1802-4325 are two exports; row 1801 repeats the header under other names'). Add a succession detector: in each dimension column, find values whose date ranges or segments are disjoint and meet at the same boundary, and batch them into one question ('At the switch around Mar 1 these labels change: Online Store -> Web Store, Popup -> Pop-Up, Complete -> Fulfilled, Cancelled -> Canceled. Same things?'). Rank alias candidates by evidence (disjoint periods, case or spacing differences), not row count. Filter answered ids before capping. Reject pairs that differ by a whole word (Southwest/Southeast).

facts.fact: F3 Channel CS means customer-service replacement shipments (warranty reships, mostly Ridgeline 2P tents since early April). They are logged at full price, but nobody paid, so they are not sales.
facts.question: None. The closest was R2 Q2 'Which orders should stay out of sales? (a Voids and cancelled, b Test and staff, c Gift card sales, d Wholesale or catering)', which has no replacement, warranty or comp option. R2 Q1 asked about channel fees, not what the channels are.
facts.data_signal: Channel 'CS' has 124 lines plus 1 'CS ' with a trailing space. It is a two-letter acronym among multi-word labels. Its rows behave differently from the rest: 0 of 125 have a discount vs 17% of other lines; 0 are Refunded or Cancelled vs about 10% elsewhere; 94% are at exactly the Products retail price. Volume runs 7 to 11 lines a month Nov to Mar, then 22, 23 and 36 in Apr, May and Jun. 49 of the 81 Apr to Jun CS lines are Ridgeline 2P Tent, and none before April. Those 49 are half of Ridgeline 2P's 94 Apr to Jun lines and add about $16.1k, enough to make it the top product (27,539 with CS vs Talus 45L 16,859). All 8 answers named Ridgeline 2P.
facts.root_cause: interview._code_questions only covers columns that profile._semantic marked as codes (average length <= 6 and 60% upper-case values), so one cryptic value in a wordy column is invisible. It also skips any column a playbook question references (channel_fees has mixed_values:channel), and its _UNIT_CODES list contains 'CS' (read as 'case'). The leave_out options are a fixed playbook list with no 'replacements/warranty/comps' option and no way to point at a value of Channel or Status. No detector compares one value's rows with the rest (discount rate, refund rate, product concentration, surge at a date).
facts.code_refs: sheetbrain/interview.py _code_questions (320-363: codes gate 333, playbook-role suppression 339-341, _UNIT_CODES 347 and 366-367); sheetbrain/profile.py _semantic codes flag (271-275); playbooks/sales_transactions.json questions.leave_out options
facts.general_fix: Add a per-value outlier detector for dimension columns. For each value with >= 20 rows, compare its rows with the rest on discount share, refund/cancel share, price vs reference price, concentration in one item and monthly trend, and also flag values that are cryptic next to their siblings. Ask with the evidence: 'What is CS in Channel? 125 lines, never discounted or refunded; 49 are Ridgeline 2P tents since April.' Options: real sales channel / not a sale (replacement, warranty, internal) / other. Make the exclusion question data-driven: its options are the actual values of the channel-like and status-like columns, plus free text. Drop the role-based suppression in _code_questions (a fee question does not explain codes) and apply unit-code skipping only in unit-of-measure columns.

facts.fact: F4 Status meanings: Exchanged (customer swapped, store kept the money), Complete, Fulfilled, Shipped, Backorder and Backordered count as sales. Refunded, Cancelled and Canceled do not.
facts.question: Only through generic options: R1 Q3 sale_def (picked 'Refunds and returns') and R2 Q2 leave_out (picked 'Voids and cancelled orders'). No question listed the Status values. The notes: 'Left out of sales, per the owner: voids and cancelled orders and gift card sales.' and 'Sales, as the owner counts them, leave out: discounts and comps and refunds and returns.' Nothing says Exchanged, Shipped or Backordered count, and 'returns' pushes readers to drop Exchanged.
facts.data_signal: Status holds 8 real values plus the stray header: Fulfilled 1,967; Complete 1,523; Refunded 270; Shipped 196; Exchanged 180; Cancelled 84; Canceled 82; Backordered 18. The tool computed this (insight mixed:status) and wrote it to the brain, but no question hangs off it. 3 answers dropped Exchanged (Feb 23,099.64). 3 dropped Backordered. 4 asked the owner to confirm exchanges or backorders.
facts.root_cause: The sales_transactions playbook has no question about which status values count. findings.finding_questions has no branch for mixed:* insights. The sale_def and leave_out options are generic concepts, and rules.exclusions never maps an option pick to actual Status values, so the notes never name real values.
facts.code_refs: playbooks/sales_transactions.json questions (no status question; mixed:status only in insights); sheetbrain/findings.py finding_questions (55-346, no mixed branch); sheetbrain/recipes.py mixed (236-250); sheetbrain/rules.py exclusions (25-59)
facts.general_fix: For any lifecycle or status-like dimension (a role of kind status, or values that match lifecycle words), ask a data-driven multi-select: 'Which of these Status values count as a sale?' listing the actual values. When there are more than 4, group them by the label families from the succession detector and accept free text. Store the answer as explicit include and exclude lists, and have the brain state them word for word ('Counts: Complete, Fulfilled, Shipped, Exchanged, Backordered. Does not count: Refunded, Cancelled, Canceled').

facts.fact: F5 Gift cards (SKUs starting GC-) are not product sales and are left out of both sales and discount numbers.
facts.question: R2 Q2 leave_out, option c 'Gift card sales'. The note says 'Left out of sales, per the owner: ... gift card sales'. It is not tied to the GC- SKUs and says nothing about discount totals.
facts.data_signal: 95 lines have SKU GC-025, GC-050 or GC-100 (Product 'Gift Card $25/$50/$100'). In Products, Category 'Gift Cards' covers exactly those 3 SKUs, and Unit Cost is blank on exactly those 3. SKU joins Products at 99.98%, so the link was already computed.
facts.root_cause: rules.exclusions builds filters only from a finding question's 'exclude' metadata or from value names in free text. A playbook option pick (gift_cards, voids) is never matched to data values. Replaying the recorded answers returns exclusions == {} and not_items == set(), so Analysis.apply_answers did nothing. No 'Totals without ...' note was written, and the counted notes (Discount sum, Unit Price sum, Status mix) still include those lines.
facts.code_refs: sheetbrain/rules.py exclusions (25-59); sheetbrain/analyze.py apply_answers (88-113); sheetbrain/brain.py _exclusion_facts (344-384, never reached)
facts.general_fix: Give each exclusion option a value matcher (patterns such as gift ?card, void|cancel, test, staff|employee, wholesale). Search every dimension, ID and category column in the workbook and follow computed joins (Products.Category 'Gift Cards' -> SKUs GC-025/050/100). Then confirm in one follow-up: 'I will leave out 95 lines with SKU GC-025, GC-050, GC-100 (Category Gift Cards) from sales and discounts. Right?' Store the concrete filter so counted notes are recomputed and a with/without note is written.

facts.fact: Net sales = qty x unit price minus the discount in dollars, over lines that are real sales. Discount totals are the dollar value on those same lines.
facts.question: R1 Q3 'When you say sales, what does that number leave out?' (picked discounts, refunds). The note is 'Sales ... leave out: discounts and comps and refunds and returns'. There is no formula, and nothing says discount totals use the same line filters.
facts.data_signal: The sheet has no amount column, only Qty, Unit Price and Discount, so every total is derived. The playbook's measure insights (pareto:net_sales:product, top_share:net_sales:channel, negatives:net_sales) need a net_sales role, found none, and produced nothing. Two answers gave discount totals that included Refunded and Cancelled lines.
facts.root_cause: sale_def asks what is left out, not how the number is built. The playbook assumes a net_sales or total column exists. When one does not, no derived measure is proposed or confirmed, and no product or month insight is computed under the owner's rules.
facts.code_refs: playbooks/sales_transactions.json insights (all measure recipes keyed on net_sales) and questions.sale_def; sheetbrain/recipes.py pareto/top_share (126-184)
facts.general_fix: When a table has quantity, price and an adjustment column but no amount column, propose a derived measure and its scope as one confirm question: 'Net sales = Qty x Unit Price minus Discount (in dollars), on the lines that count as sales; discount totals use the same lines. Right?' Then run the measure recipes (by month, product, channel) on the derived measure with the owner's filters, so the brain carries counted numbers that follow the rules.

facts.fact: Some old prices came through as text like $179.00. They are just the number.
facts.question: None
facts.data_signal: 42 Unit Price cells are text such as '$179.00', '$329.00', '$24.00', all on KH- rows (10 Nov, 21 Dec, 5 Jan, 5 Feb, 1 Mar). profile_column counted numeric_text=42, but the column is typed number (99% numeric). The node's sum ($389.0k = 389,012.42) silently skips these 42 lines.
facts.root_cause: analyze._table_insights raises numbers_as_text only when the column type is text and at least half its cells are numeric text, so a mostly numeric column with some text never triggers it. profile_column sums only int/float values.
facts.code_refs: sheetbrain/analyze.py _table_insights (344-351); sheetbrain/profile.py profile_column (166-190)
facts.general_fix: No question needed: code can settle it. In any numeric column, parse currency-formatted text as numbers, include it in sums, and write a counted fact ('42 Unit Price cells are text like $179.00; they are read as numbers'). A reader then knows to coerce them and not drop them.

facts.fact: The Products tab's Retail is today's price (some prices rose at the platform move). What was charged is the Unit Price on each order line.
facts.question: None
facts.data_signal: The Products title reads 'SKU list (retail as of May 2026)'. 344 of 4,320 lines have Unit Price different from Products Retail (335 of them KH- lines). 9 SKUs step up in price at the switch (Ridgeline 3P 399 -> 409, Talus 45L 179 -> 189, Basecamp 6P 549 -> 569, Alder 20F 289 -> 299 ...).
facts.root_cause: The SKU join to Products is band 'auto' (99.98%), but no detector compares a looked-up price with the row's own price, and no question asks which price is authoritative.
facts.code_refs: sheetbrain/profile.py find_joins (384-449); sheetbrain/analyze.py (no price-vs-reference recipe); sheetbrain/recipes.py (spread compares prices across entities, not against a reference table)
facts.general_fix: For any automatic join where both sides have a price-like metric, compute the share of rows where they differ and whether the gap steps at a date. Write it as a counted fact ('Unit Price differs from Products Retail on 344 lines, mostly before Mar 2; Products holds one current price per SKU'). When the owner's goal involves revenue, ask once which price reflects what was charged.

misleading_notes.note: [said per owner] Rows that repeat a Order ID: different, keep both, per the owner. Together with [counted] 1,111 Order ID values appear more than once (2,721 rows).
misleading_notes.effect: Readers took it as 'no deduplication needed' and kept the 55 # migration copies. Six of the 8 answers' Feb figures reproduce only with the copies kept (24,702.64 / 23,099.64). Judges: 'explicitly says no deduplication' (luna r2), 'Treated repeated order numbers as separate items and kept the Feb 27-Mar 1 # duplicates' (opus r2), 'retaining order lines by Order ID does not resolve these duplicates' (sonnet r2).
misleading_notes.cause: recipes.duplicates flagged single-column ID repeats while ignoring the tool's own composite key (Order ID + SKU is unique). findings.py framed that as 'the same one twice?'. The fact template then stored the answer as a blanket rule about repeated IDs.
misleading_notes.fix: Suppress the ID-repeat finding when a composite key explains it. Keep grain notes narrow ('repeats because each row is one line of an order'). Detect content duplicates under different IDs separately, and state that result (or 'not checked') in the brain.

misleading_notes.note: [said per owner] Sales, as the owner counts them, leave out: discounts and comps and refunds and returns.
misleading_notes.effect: 'Returns' led readers to drop Exchanged lines, which the owner counts as sales. luna r1, luna r2 and haiku r1 all produced Feb 23,099.64, which reproduces with Exchanged dropped (discounts 8,954.13 / 8,907.93). 'Comps' fed unsupported staff-comp explanations. The owner never said comps or returns: they picked two option letters.
misleading_notes.cause: The playbook's option labels bundle extra words ('Discounts and comps', 'Refunds and returns'). interview.fill/_in_sentence write the whole label into the owner's sentence.
misleading_notes.fix: Use one concept per option and render only what the owner picked. When a picked concept overlaps real values (returns vs Exchanged/Refunded), ask a follow-up that lists those values.

misleading_notes.note: [said per owner] Left out of sales, per the owner: voids and cancelled orders and gift card sales.
misleading_notes.effect: The note names no real Status values, so readers guessed at the rest. luna r2, haiku r1 and haiku r2 dropped Backordered (haiku r1 j2: 'Misstates the owner's rule as excluding incomplete or non-delivered orders'). luna r1, opus r1, sonnet r1 and sonnet r2 asked the owner to confirm exchanges and backorders, which the owner had already settled.
misleading_notes.cause: A generic playbook option with no link to the Status column (rules.exclusions ignores option picks) and no positive list of what counts.
misleading_notes.fix: Use a data-driven Status question and store explicit include and exclude value lists, stated word for word in the note.

misleading_notes.note: [counted] Channel splits sales into Web Store, Online Store and Marketplace and more; delivery-app orders often carry commissions the sales figure does not show.
misleading_notes.effect: It gave a restaurant rule of thumb the authority of a counted fact. luna r1/r2 and sonnet r1 raised delivery-channel commissions and marketplace fees the brief does not support. It also lists Web Store and Online Store as separate channels when they are one channel under two names.
misleading_notes.cause: brain._gotcha_facts marks any playbook gotcha whose template has a {values:} slot as source 'computed', status 'current'. Filling in values from the data turned a guess into a 'counted' note. The text is restaurant-specific, and the owner's 'not sure' on fees does not retire it.
misleading_notes.fix: Set provenance by what the sentence claims: a playbook rule of thumb is always a guess, whatever slots it fills. Guesses enter the file only when a data detector supports them. Pick gotcha wording by business subtype (e-commerce vs restaurant).

misleading_notes.note: [guess, unconfirmed] Discount can mix promotions with comps. Comps are items given away by staff; promotions are offers to customers.
misleading_notes.effect: Answers explained discounts as employee comps (luna r1 and r2: 'Claims discounts combine promotions and employee comps without supporting evidence'). Meanwhile the real Discount problem, percent before Mar 2 and dollars after, went unmentioned.
misleading_notes.cause: A playbook gotcha fires on has_role:discount alone, with no evidence check.
misleading_notes.fix: Evidence-gate gotchas (e.g. only when some lines are discounted to 100%). Otherwise keep them off the file.

misleading_notes.note: [guess, unconfirmed] Online exports often stamp times in UTC, so late-evening sales can fall on the next calendar day.
misleading_notes.effect: luna r1 and r2 raised UTC shifts the judges called unsupported.
misleading_notes.cause: The gotcha fires on has_role:order_date alone. The tool never looked at the real time signal: KH- rows carry times of day, # rows are midnight-only. That is a two-systems clue, not a UTC problem.
